# Copilot Instructions for Michel Decision OS\n\n## Core Principles\n\n1. **TypeScript Strict Mode**: Always use strict mode. Never use `any` to hide errors.\n2. **No Invented Data**: Never create fake market prices, company metrics, news, or financial data.\n3. **Test Everything**: Every calculation must be tested. Verify both happy path and edge cases.\n4. **No Secrets in Client**: API keys must never appear in browser bundles or frontend code.\n5. **Preserve Functionality**: Check existing code before making changes. Prevent regressions.\n6. **Accessibility First**: WCAG 2.1 AA. Keyboard navigation, screen readers, sufficient contrast.\n7. **Clear Terminology**: Use full words instead of cryptic abbreviations (\"portfolio\" not \"pf\").\n8. **Run All Checks**: After changes, execute: lint, typecheck, test, and build.\n9. **Document Formulas**: Every calculation must be documented with formula and interpretation.\n10. **Handle Errors Gracefully**: Show users what went wrong, never swallow errors silently.\n\n## Data Handling\n\n- All user data is stored locally in IndexedDB by default\n- No telemetry, tracking, or external data transmission without explicit user action\n- Missing data must be clearly marked as \"Not available\"\n- Confidence scores must reflect data quality\n- Never suppress warnings about incomplete data\n\n## Code Style\n\n- Use functional components with hooks\n- Prefer composition over inheritance\n- Keep components focused and small\n- Use Zustand for global state (not context)\n- Use Zod for runtime validation of all external data\n- Use Dexie for IndexedDB abstraction\n\n## Calculations\n\n- All financial calculations must be deterministic\n- Monte Carlo simulations must support configurable random seeds\n- Use explicit formulas in comments\n- Test against known values\n- Handle currency conversions explicitly\n\n## UI/UX\n\n- Responsive design: mobile first, then tablet, then desktop\n- Clear visual hierarchy\n- No decorative gradients or unnecessary animations\n- Tooltips for all complex metrics\n- Error messages must be specific and actionable\n- Loading states must be visible\n- Confirmation dialogs for destructive actions\n\n## Imports and Exports\n\n- Always validate imported data before storage\n- Show preview before committing imports\n- Detect and handle duplicates\n- Never overwrite valid data with corrupted imports\n- Support multiple formats (CSV, JSON, encrypted backup)\n- Version schema for migrations\n\n## Git Practices\n\n- Write clear commit messages\n- Link to issues when relevant\n- Keep commits focused and small\n- Rebase before merge, don't create merge commits\n\n## When in Doubt\n\n- Check the documentation in `docs/`\n- Look at existing patterns in the codebase\n- Run tests to verify behavior\n- Ask only about security-critical decisions or impossible technical choices\n
